name: Espresso machine
description: Hot water under pressure passes through a tightly packed bed of ground coffee and produces a concentrated drink in a short time.
steps: Grind the beans finely and measure the dose.
Distribute the coffee evenly in the portafilter and tamp it.
Lock the portafilter into the group and start the extraction.
Stop the extraction once you have the desired amount and serve immediately.

name: Pour-over (V60)
description: A filter method where hot water is slowly poured over ground coffee in a dripper with a paper filter. The cup tastes clean and clear.
steps: Place the filter in the dripper, rinse it with hot water and discard the water.
Add the ground coffee and level the surface.
Wet the coffee with a small amount of water and wait 30–45 seconds.
Slowly pour the remaining water in circles in several stages.
Wait until the water drains through and serve.

name: French press
description: An immersion method: coffee steeps in hot water in a carafe, then a plunger with a mesh filter separates the grounds. The result is rich with a noticeable body.
steps: Grind the coffee coarsely and add it to the carafe.
Pour hot water over it so that all the grounds are wet.
Cover with the lid without pressing the plunger and wait about 4 minutes.
Slowly press the plunger down.
Pour the coffee into cups right away so it does not over-extract on the grounds.

name: AeroPress
description: A compact device in which coffee steeps with water and is then pressed through a filter with a plunger. Parameters depend heavily on the chosen recipe, so only general steps are given here.
steps: Insert the filter into the cap and rinse it with hot water.
Add the ground coffee to the chamber.
Add water and stir.
Insert the plunger and wait for the time given in your recipe.
Press slowly until you hear the hiss of air.

name: Moka pot
description: A pot in which steam pressure pushes hot water up through ground coffee. The result is strong and concentrated, but it is not true espresso because the pressure is much lower.
steps: Fill the bottom chamber with water up to the safety valve.
Fill the funnel with coffee and level it without tamping.
Screw on the top part tightly.
Place it on low or medium heat with the lid open.
When the coffee stops rising, remove it from the heat and serve.
